title: Power BI for breweries, delivered by role and owned by you
standfirst: Your head brewer should not be learning report design. A brewery needs the right numbers in front of each role every morning, agreed once, running in its own tenant.
description: Power BI for breweries delivered as a service: role pages for brewing, packaging, quality and finance in your own tenant, with numbers that agree.

sections.h2: Why brewery dashboards stop being opened

blocks.p: Power BI for breweries usually starts the same way. Someone senior asks for a production dashboard. A report appears with forty visuals on one page. It gets opened for a fortnight. Then the head brewer goes back to the whiteboard in the cellar office, because the whiteboard is right and the dashboard is a day late.

The software was rarely the problem. The problem is that nobody agreed what the numbers mean. Packaging counts production at the filler. Finance counts it at the excise register. The brewhouse counts cast wort. All three call it production, so the morning meeting spends ten minutes on whose figure is right before anyone talks about beer.

A brewery does not need to become a Power BI shop to fix this. What it needs is a set of pages, one per role, that answer the question each person asks before the morning meeting, from definitions that production and finance have both signed. That is something we deliver and run. It is not a course your team has to sit.

sections.h2: What each role sees and decides differently

blocks.p: This is the set we put in front of a mid-sized brewery. Each page carries six or seven numbers at most. Each number clicks through to the batch behind it, then to the tank, then to the readings.

What they see each morning

Extract and knockout gravity against target per brew, cast volume against plan

blocks.p: The plant director gets one more page with the handful of numbers that move money: cost per packaged hectolitre, loss by stage, OEE on the bottleneck line, stock cover on the top SKUs, open quality holds. If the director has to ring the cellar to find out why loss went up, the page has failed, however good it looks.

sections.h2: A worked example: one shift, two OEE figures

blocks.p: Say a can line is planned for an 8-hour shift, 480 minutes. It stops for 60 minutes in total, 30 of them for a planned CIP. Rated speed is 600 cans a minute. It makes 226,800 cans, of which 223,400 pass fill level and seam checks.

head: Factor
CIP counted as lost time
CIP taken out of planned time
rows: Availability
Performance
Quality
OEE

blocks.p: Both figures are arithmetically correct. If packaging quotes one and finance quotes the other, the meeting loses fifteen minutes and nobody fixes the filler. The cure is not a better chart. It is one written decision, made by the people who own the line and the budget, on whether planned cleaning counts as lost time. Once it is signed, every page in the building uses it and the argument does not come back.

Most of the real work in a brewery dashboard project is decisions like that one. Rated speed per SKU, because a line validated at 600 cans a minute on 330 ml may run slower on 500 ml. Which loss belongs to which stage. Whether a blend counts as one batch or two. We bring the list of decisions. Your people make them.

sections.h2: Questions to ask any provider before you buy brewery dashboards

ul: **Whose tenant does it run in?** If the reports live in the provider's account, you are renting your own numbers.
**Who signs the definitions?** Production and finance should sign them, not the developer.
**Can every number click through to a batch?** If it cannot, nobody will trust it the first time it looks odd.
**How current is each page?** Every page should show when each source last loaded.
**What will licences and capacity cost each year?** Get that in writing, separate from the project fee.
**Who changes a page when your process changes?** Ask how long it takes and what it costs.
**What happens when you leave?** You should keep every report, model and record without a migration.

sections.h2: How Beer365 delivers Power BI for a brewery

blocks.p: Beer365 is beer intelligence for the whole beer business, built by Disruptive Advantage. It runs inside your own Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Fabric tenant. It reads from the systems you already have, whether that is Excel, the ERP, SCADA, the historian or the LIMS. It never writes back to control. Brewhouse, cellar, packaging, quality, plant, supply chain, sales and finance meet in one batch record. The role pages read from that record, so the head brewer and the finance director quote the same number.

ul: **Assessment, two weeks, fixed price.** We look at the roles, the questions they ask and the systems that hold the answers. You see which pages come first and which Microsoft licences you will need.
**Proof of concept, 20 weeks.** The first pages run on your data against a baseline you sign at the start. Each month your plant controller signs a statement of where the number stands against it.
**Live.** The pages become the morning meeting. Questions asked of the copilot in plain English return the same numbers, with the batch and tag cited.

blocks.p: You own every report, model and record. From your IT team we need a Microsoft tenant with Fabric capacity, read-only access to the source systems and one named person who can open doors. Nobody in the brewery has to learn report design.

faq.q: Do we need Power BI licences?
faq.a: Yes, in your own name, because Beer365 runs in your own Microsoft tenant. Which licences you need and how much Fabric capacity depend on how many people read the pages. The two-week assessment sets that out with costs before you commit.

faq.q: Do our people need to learn Power BI?
faq.a: No. They open pages and ask questions. We build and run what sits behind them. If your team wants to build its own reports later, the governed model is yours to build on.

faq.q: Who owns the dashboards if we stop working with you?
faq.a: You do. Every report, model and record sits in your tenant from the first day. Nothing has to be moved or handed back.

faq.q: Can Beer365 change settings on our plant?
faq.a: No. It reads from your ERP, SCADA, historian, LIMS and spreadsheets. It never writes back to control.
